answer: Give each identity a verifiable-delay-function ageing pass: registration starts a sequential computation no parallel hardware can shorten, verified by any peer in milliseconds and recorded on-chain. Full earning rights arrive only after 14 days of ageing; fresh identities earn nothing. Forging 100 identities costs 100 separate runs, about 1,400 days of single-thread compute, and 1,000 fakes need 14,000 days. The proof is a bridge from registration to trust, a crystal-clear cipher of elapsed time no clone can copy. Duplicates restart the clock, so cloning buys delay, not income.
